question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+y{e}^{x}) \\  & =2x\cdot {y}^{2}+y\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =2x{y}^{2}+y{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}+y{e}^{x}) \\  & =2x\cdot 2y+1\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =4xy+{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{xyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{xy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy+{e}^{x}) \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot y+{e}^{x} \\  & =4y+{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$
